subject: Confirming non-training assurances and archival/backup exceptions
messages:
From: Tom Walker <security@finhealth.com>
To: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-22 10:12 AM PDT
Subject: Confirm: will customer data be used for model training? + archival exceptions

Hi Avery,

Quick question from our security review: can you confirm the current Redwood position on model training using customer text? Our legal team needs a concise assurance we can include in our vendor assessment. Specific follow-ups:

- Is customer text ever used to improve or train models (online or offline)?
- Do any internal logs, debug snapshots, or backup archives contain customer text that could be used for training?
- If you say no, are there carve-outs (e.g., debug snapshots retained for 30 days, disaster recovery backups) we should be aware of?

We'd appreciate a short, plain-language statement and any pointers to an attestation or evidence we can attach to our risk file.

Thanks,
Tom Walker
Head of Security Operations
FinHealth

From: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
To: Tom Walker <security@finhealth.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-06-22 12:03 PM PDT
Subject: Re: Confirm: will customer data be used for model training? + archival exceptions

Tom —

Thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: Redwood does not use customer text from production inference to train general-purpose models. Below is a compact statement you can include in your assessment, plus clarifications on the edge cases you flagged. Mina (security) and Priyom (product security) are looped in for the formal attestation and backup specifics.

Suggested plain-language statement (feel free to copy into your vendor doc):
"Redwood Inference does not use or incorporate customer-provided text from hosted inference requests to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve its general-purpose models. Customer request payloads are treated as customer-controlled data and are excluded from model training pipelines. Operational telemetry may be collected for debugging and service health, but customer text is excluded from any training dataset ingestion processes."

Clarifications / nuance:
- Snapshots and backups: We maintain operational snapshots for debugging and disaster recovery. These are short-lived by default (configurable TTL) and are not fed into training pipelines. For customers requiring stronger guarantees we offer options to reduce snapshot TTLs or exclude certain routes.
- Debug artifacts: Ephemeral debug logs that contain customer text are retained behind strict access controls and are purged on a 30-day default; this window can be tightened under contract.
- KV/prefix caches: Caches used for inference are memory-resident and not persisted to long-term training stores; eviction and TTL behavior is documented in the retention matrix (attached).
- Derivative models / internal research: Any internal experiments that require training data are performed only on synthetic or opt-in datasets that do not include customer production requests unless explicit consent is provided.

I attached our latest attestation draft (no_training_attestation_v1.pdf) and a snapshot/retention matrix for your legal/security team to review. Mina — would you mind confirming the exact language we can sign and if we can provide a signed attestation PDF for FinHealth?

Best,
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jun 22, 2025 at 12:03 PM Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com> wrote:
> Tom —
> 
> Thanks for the clear list. Short answer up front: Redwood does not use customer text from production inference to train general-purpose models.

Hi Tom — thanks for the question. I'll add a few precise commitments that our compliance team can stand behind and that should map cleanly into your vendor risk template.

Canonical commitments we can provide (we can sign these in an attestation):
1) No training: Redwood attests that customer-inferred text submitted to hosted or dedicated inference endpoints is not ingested into model training datasets, either for our hosted models or for any internal general-purpose model improvement processes.
2) Snapshot/backups: Production backups and operational snapshots may contain request payloads for short-term operational purposes (debugging, RCA, DR). These artifacts are covered by strict IAM controls and are not used for training. Default retention is 30 days for debug snapshots and 90 days for DR backups; both are configurable under enterprise contracts.
3) Access & auditing: Any access to artifacts containing customer text is logged, audited, and restricted to a small set of engineers under break-glass controls. Audit logs are available for review during on-site audits or via SOC 2 evidence packages.
4) Contract carve-outs: If a customer requires zero retention of request text anywhere in operational snapshots/backups, we can offer a configuration that tombstones raw request payloads immediately and routes observability to anonymized metrics only.

I will attach a signed attestation PDF (final) once legal signs off. In the meantime the attached attestation draft is accurate for most customers. Priyom — please confirm there are no outstanding legal caveats before I finalize.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
